THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT,
PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 20.01.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.338/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE COURT OF THE II ADDITIONAL MACT AND ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE, BIDAR SITTING AT BHALKI AND ALLOW THIS APPEAL BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT FROM RS.5,63,000/- TO RS.14,00,000/- ONLY AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANTS BEFORE THE TRIBUNAL, PASS AN ORDER AS TO THE COSTS OF THIS APPEAL AND ETC.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT MFA No.200961/2018 is filed by the insurer challenging the entitlement of the claimants for the compensation awarded by the II Additional MACT and Additional District Judge, Bidar sitting at Bhalki (henceforth referred as 'the Tribunal'), in MVC No.338/2016, vide judgment and award dated 20.01.2018.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1251 2. MFA No.201053/2018 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded in the aforesaid case.
3. The claimants/respondents are the legal heirs of deceased Subhash Mahada, aged 54 years and an agriculturist.

The claimants claimed that the deceased died in a road traffic accident while he was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No.MH.24.AK.0897 which was dashed against by a bus belonging to the North-East Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (henceforth referred as 'Corporation') bearing registration No.KA.32.F.1669.

The claimants clamed that they were dependent on the earnings of the deceased and hence, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.64,48,000/- from the Corporation.
4. The claim petition was opposed by the Corporation, who denied that the claimants were dependent on the deceased.

sentences.text: The Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence, held that the claimants were dependent on the deceased and that the accident happened due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus belonging to the Corporation.

The Tribunal considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and deducted 1/3rd towards his personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation:
Sl.No. Heads Amount i. Loss of dependency Rs.5,28,000/-
ii. Loss of estate Rs.20,000/-
iii. Transportation of dead Rs.15,000/-
 body
The Tribunal directed the Corporation to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and award, NC: 2023:KHC-K:1251 the Corporation as well as the claimants are in separate appeals.
7. Learned counsel for the Corporation contended that the claimants being the sons of the deceased were not dependant on the deceased as they were all majors by age.
Hence, he contended that the Tribunal could not have awarded any compensation towards loss of dependency.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the claimants contended that the accident happened on 23.05.2016 and this Court had consistently considered the notional income of a person dying or injured in a road traffic accident in the year 2016 at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month.
He also contended that the Tribunal must have added loss of future prospects at 10% since the deceased was 54 years old.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
The accident that happened on 23.05.2016 is not in dispute.
The age and avocation of the deceased is also not in dispute.
The claimants were 28 years and 26 years respectively and both of them claimed to be unemployed.
This therefore meant that they were dependent on the earnings of the deceased from cultivating the land belonging to the family.

Therefore, the contention of the Mahada Siddeshwar And Anr vs The Divisional Controller on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177394010/
4 learned counsel for the corporation that there were no proof of dependency is without any basis.

sentences.text: The Tribunal was right in holding that the claimants were dependent on the deceased.

Even otherwise,
in view of the judgment in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birender and Others1, the claimants cannot be entitled for the compensation on the mere ground that they were all majors by age.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Birender and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the appeal filed by the corporation does not merit consideration.

11. In so far as the appeal for enhancement of the compensation is concerned, this Court had applied the AIR 2020 SC 434 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1251 notional income of a person dying or injured in a road traffic accident in the year 2016 at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month.
In addition, the claimants were entitled to loss of future prospects at 10% of the notional income.
Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation under the head loss of dependency.
They were also entitled to loss of parental consortium as held by the Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Versus Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others2.

 Rs.9,625/- - Rs.3,208/-
 (1/3rd) = Rs.6,417/- x  12 x 11 = 8,47,044/-)
 2. Loss of parental Rs.88,000/-

In view of the above, the appeal filed by the Corporation is dismissed and the appeal filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation is allowed in part.

sentences.text: The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.5,63,000/- to Rs.9,68,044/-.
The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.

The insurer of the offending vehicle shall deposit the enhanced compensation and interest before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of a receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be kept in the names of the claimants in equal portion in any Nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
Any amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
